# Lebanese Arabizi style guide

Quotes are Christina's rulings, word for word, tagged with the date of the note they come from (rulings_source.md and phrasing_source.md are the full notes). "[flagged: ...]" marks a ruling kept as written that needs her decision or sits next to another ruling. The reply forms, speaker words, accepted and rejected spellings and number words are in forms.json; approved answers in examples.jsonl (its first line is a header).

## 1. Who decides

Christina, the app's owner, is the native Lebanese Arabizi speaker and the only judge of Arabizi here. Every Arabizi word in this guide is quoted from her rulings (rulings_source.md, phrasing_source.md) or exported from tables she approved (forms.json). Where a ruling says it corrects or reverses an earlier one, the later one stands. Do not invent, extend or "correct" Arabizi beyond what is here.

- (undated) she is the native speaker judging the dataset; wrong grammar teaches the model bad Arabizi.
- (undated) I am not a native speaker and my own Arabizi is unreliable; prefer her seeds and her corrected sentences, and ask her to review anything new before it enters training.
- (2026-11-14) (the batch 1 ban on "shu sert sarfe" was wrong)
- (2026-11-23) **"eshhor" is fine** (her, reversing 2026-11-19): taken off the rejected list.

## 2. Register and language mixing

Replies are short, friendly Lebanese Arabizi (or English, or natural mixing, following the user). The reply takes the user's gender; the exact approved forms are in forms.json.

- (2026-11-16) Mixed lines must be natural code-switching ("what can you do badle?"), never word-for-word halves like "shu can you do".
- (2026-11-20) Mixed "what was the price": **shu ken the price / shu el price** (never "shu was").
- (2026-11-16) Mixed: "I wanna know wayn sarafet / wain dafa3et last month" (NOT "wayn ra7o masarife").
- (2026-11-18) Assistant replies take the user's gender: se3dak (m) / se3dik (f), bse3dak / bse3dik, masarifak / masarifik, masrufak / masrufik, baddak / baddik.
- (2026-11-18) Friends: 3 of 5 prefer sentences that avoid "you" when gender is unknown.
- (2026-11-18) "tehki" / "tehke" ("aam tehki" = you're talking about) are the same for a man and a woman: not gendered.
- (2026-11-18) Neutral drops "you": "fie jeweb 3an el masruf men el fwatir", "aymta w mn aya mahal?".
- (2026-11-18) The assistant may talk about itself ("Mnih, merci", "Kel shi tamam"); emojis allowed but rarely; "salam" fine; users call it by name ("hii fatourati").
- (2026-11-18) Thanks replies: Ahla w Sahla, Walaw, Ya Hala, Ta3a kel yom, "3a rase / 3a rasi" (friends); NOT "El 3afu" (friends rated it 1-2).
- (2026-11-17) Prefer the most common Lebanese greetings/replies (kifak/kifik, shu el akhbar, etc.).
- (2026-11-20) Approved from her word bank: ahlen, hamdella, meshe el 7al, 3a rase (neutral "aa rase"), wala yhemmak/yhemmik, tekram 3aynak/3aynik, es2alne/es2aline, eh walla, allah y3inak/y3inik, ya latif, ma3 el salame, nshoufak/nshoufik; not well: salamtak/salamtik, "inshalla kel shi bi sir a7san", alla y2awik/y2awike, ma3lesh.
- (2026-11-19) Approved answer style: "about" = "ya3ne ta2riban"; dates "9 December 2026"; answers repeat the item and period ("Dafa3te 710,000 LBP (ya3ne ta2riban $7.93) la Allo Taxi hal shaher."); "you spent/paid" f sarafte / dafa3te, m sarafet / dafa3et, neutral "El masruf ... :" / "Masarif ...:"
- (2026-11-20) Agent-written answers: all 40 approved, incl. zero results ("ma jebte X", "Ma fi wala fatoura men X", "Wala shi, ma jebte X"), nafs el se3er, sar, kamen, bel dollar, w bas, "ma ba3ref eza arkhas aw aghla", "b $2.10".
- (2026-11-19) "zoret" = visited (formal): keep it rare, prefer rehet / ro7t / 3am ruh.
- (2026-11-16) mlakhas / molakhas correct but very formal (mlakhas more used)
- (2026-11-14) Usual/average: 3adatan / aadatan / bel 3ade far more common than moyenne; motawassit is not used.
- (2026-11-18) **bs = bas** (interchangeable) [resolved 2026-11-23: the model must understand both; questions say "bs" about a quarter of the time]

## 3. Spelling rules and never-use forms

Accepted variants and every rejected spelling the code enforces are in forms.json ("spellings"); a rejected spelling never appears in a reply. Her spelling rulings:

- (2026-11-20) **Stop doubling letters**: most people type 2ale (not 2alle), sajalto / sajalte / msajal (not sajjalto ...); single letters in most words.
- (2026-11-22) Double letters: avoid (khaberne, tale3le), a few are fine.
- (2026-11-20) Prefer **fwatirak / fwatirik** over fawatirak / fawatirik. [resolved 2026-11-23: fawatirak / fawatirik are correct too, fwatirak just a bit more common: use both, fwatirak a little more often]
- (2026-11-22) **sho, mish, bokra, 2abadet are very common** (her).
- (2026-11-14) "How much": aday/adday more common than adde; also use adesh, 2adesh, addesh, adaysh, addeh. Receipts: fwatir/fwatire more common than fawatir/fawatire.
- (2026-11-14) Spelling of "I became", most to least used: sert, soret, seret, serit.
- (2026-11-16) "I bought": **jebet** and **shtrit** are common and must be used
- (2026-11-16) "shtret" was my own invention, not hers.
- (2026-11-21) **sarafet = I spent; "sarfet" is wrong**.
- (2026-11-22) **"sraft" is wrong** (her view): use sarafet.
- (2026-11-22) "fershet sean" and "shteret / ma shteret" are WRONG (her list's errors), never use.
- (2026-11-22) **retib** = salary, "el retib" = the salary; **retibe is wrong**.
- (2026-11-19) NEVER "li fet" / "li fetou" (rarely used): "that passed" = li ata3 / li ata3o / ataoo, el madi, li mara2.
- (2026-11-16) Biscuits: "biscuits" or "baskot", NEVER "baskawit". Chewing gum: **3elke** (not 3elka).
- (2026-11-15) 3ela2at = hangers (not 3alla2at)
- (2026-11-20) NEVER kallefetne / kallefoune.
- (2026-11-22) **mana2ish** = plural of **man2ushi**; "man2ish" is not a spelling anyone uses (fixed in the mix).
- (2026-11-15) NEVER "taba3 el gazoz": say soda, or mashroubet ghazie (formal).
- (2026-11-15) ("sarle shtri" is absolutely wrong)
- (2026-11-19) "how much sarle spent 3al X" is WRONG: say "how much defe3 / def3a 3al X".
- (2026-11-21) NEVER "sa7abit menne"
- (2026-11-21) NEVER "adde ra7 men jaybte" (use aday sarafet 3a X). NEVER "emta bekhlas ma3ashe".
- (2026-11-16) Sponge: "safra jale" is NOT a word; say **sfenjet jale** or **sponge jale**.
- (2026-11-22) Medicines: **edewye / 2edewye** (not adwye).
- (2026-11-20) "b7al hada / bhal hada" is NOT Lebanese.
- (2026-11-22) "Carefour" is her spelling of Carrefour.

- Batch-1 rules (2026-11-21, batch1_cleanup.py; marked * = also applied to every stored question by fixes.QUESTION_RULES):
  - *sarfet: "sarfet" (I spent) -> "sarafet" (her ruling: sarafet = I spent).

## 4. Grammar rulings

- (2026-11-14) "ekher marra" (last time) needs a past marker: "2adesh **ken** 7a2 el bantalon ekher marra", not "2adesh 7a2 ... ekher marra" (reads as "how much is it last time").
- (2026-11-16) **aday is usually a COUNT**: "aday jebet terrea", "aday aam jib / beshtere / eshtere terrea" = how many. **"bi aday jebet el X" / "bi aday aam jib el X" = the PRICE** I got it for. aday + dafa3et/sarafet/kallaf = money.
- (2026-11-16) Counting a NOUN uses **kam** + singular ("kam fetoura sajalet hal jemaa"), never "aday/adde fetoura"; aday as a count goes with a verb ("aday jebet terrea").
- (2026-11-20) **kam = only for COUNTING** things: kam marra, kam fatoura, kam ta7wile. For an amount of MONEY never kam: aday / adesh / adeysh / adde ("aday dakhle", not "kam dakhle"; "ahle aday sarafo", not "ahle kam sarafo").
- (2026-11-20) "kam dollar" is fine (counting dollars).
- (2026-11-16) "aday 3adad el fwatir…" is correct.
- (2026-11-22) "adde / aday sar 3ande fwatir" counting receipts stays. [flagged: aday before a plural noun, next to the 2026-11-16 "never aday/adde fetoura": both kept as written]
- (2026-11-19) The user's own "I" words by speaker: I paid f. def3a / defaa, m. defe3; "dafa3et / dafa3it" are the same for both. I feel f. 7esa / 7ase / hesa / hasi, m. 7eses / hasis / heses. I've been buying f. meshtreye / meshtriye, m. meshtere / meshteri. A man's question must never say def3a.
- (2026-11-16) CORRECTION to earlier note: **7eses / heses hale = masculine** (with 3ayesh / aayesh); **feminine = 7esa / hase / hesa** (with 3ayshe / aayshe).
- (2026-11-19) "I feel": woman hase / hasi / 7ase / 7asi / 7esa / hesa; man hases / 7ases / hasis / 7eses / heses.
- (2026-11-22) **"sarli defe3"** is correct (the man's form of sarli def3a).
- (2026-11-14) "So far" totals: "shu sert defe3 (m) / def3a (f) 7a2 X", "shu sert sarfe (f) / saref (m) hal jemaa" — valid and natural
- (2026-11-22) **-et before a name is NOT plural**: it is the ta marbuta of مدرسة joining the noun to a name ("saydaliyet Mazen" = Mazen's pharmacy, one shop; same for "dekkenet abou jihad"). Plural only with nothing named after it: "el saydaliyet" = the pharmacies (saydaliye / saydalie singular).
- (2026-11-16) **aal / 3al = "to THE"**: only before an unnamed place or thing ("rehet aal pharmacie", "aal furn"); before a NAMED shop use **aa / 3a** or **aand / 3and** ("rehet aa Pharmacie Nassar", "aa Pull and Bear", "aand Younes"), never "aal Pharmacie Nassar / aal Pull and Bear / 3al Cafe Younes".
- (2026-11-16) AT a place = **3and / aand** ("deyman 3and Rizk"); **3a / aa** = TO a place ("ro7t 3a Rizk"). NEVER "deyman 3a X".
- (2026-11-20) **bi = in, mn / men = since** ("bi kanoun l awal" = in December, "mn kanoun l awal" = since December). "f" is never used ("f kanoun el awal" came from batch 1's writer).
- (2026-11-15) MEANING: "adesh sarle meshtereye X" = how long since I LAST bought X (time since the last purchase), while "adde sarle 3am jib / eshtri X" (continuous) = how long have I been buying X (since the first purchase). Never use meshtreye for "since when have I been buying".
- (2026-11-19) "adde sarle defe3 3al X" means HOW LONG SINCE I paid for X, not how much so far.
- (2026-11-20) "how much have I spent on it so far": **aday sar masroufe aalay** (NEVER "adde sar le masrouf 3leh").
- (2026-11-20) **"it cost me"** (her table): past **kalafne** (masc.), **kalafetne** (fem.), **kalafoune** (pl.); participle **mkalefne** (masc.), **mkalfetne** (fem.), **mkalfini** (pl.) — "adesh/aday kalafoune".
- (2026-11-16) Tense: "3ed aday **jebet** X hal shaher" for the past/a period; "aday **aam jib** X" for now, habits, how often ("3ed aday aam jib sushi 3adatan").
- (2026-11-22) **"aam jibon" is habitual** (what I usually buy): never with ekher marra.
- (2026-11-22) Agreement: plural things -> jebton or jebta; a masculine singular (el shi, el 7elo) -> jebto; el la7me -> jebta.
- (2026-11-16) Relative clause takes the object suffix: "shu 3adad el fwatir li **sajalta**", "3adad el fwatir li / yali **hatayta**" (not "li sajalet / li hatayt"); "kam fatoura sajalet" is fine.
- (2026-11-14) "fwatir" = receipts, "fwatire" = MY receipts.
- (2026-11-14) "should" = **lezem**
- (2026-11-15) "takalif 3ande" (no -e when 3ande already shows possession).
- (2026-11-15) Future: ha / ra7
- (2026-11-15) kahraba is feminine
- (2026-11-15) Spell "ykalefne" (not ykalfene); madrase is feminine, so "tkalefne".
- (2026-11-16) "that": **eno** far more used than enni (any gender; enni still OK).
- (2026-11-16) Don't repeat the item twice in one sentence: second time use a pronoun
- (2026-11-22) "I usually order": **botlob / betlob** (both very common), NEVER "b2otlob".
- (2026-11-22) ("bjib" itself still unconfirmed.) [flagged: open: her decision needed]

## 5. Periods and numbers

- (2026-11-19) Two weeks: jem3ten / jeme3tain / jeme3ten; two months: shahrain / shahrein / shahren. This month: hal shaher / he el shaher / hayda el shaher / heda el shaher.
- (2026-11-19) Weeks plural: "3 jema3 / jme3 / jemaa" ("bel 3 jema3 el ekhrin", "ekhir 3 jme3"), NEVER "jem3at".
- (2026-11-19) "the last two weeks" = "el jeme3tein el ekhrin" (not "ekhirin"); "ekher jem3ten" also fine.
- (2026-11-23) Weeks stay "jema3 / jme3 / jemaa" (never jem3at): 3 weeks = "tlet jema3 / tlet jme3".
- (2026-11-23) Numbers before a period word: "ekher tlet shhour", "ekher arba3 shhour", "ekher 3ashr iyem" fine; 5 = **"ekher khames iyem"** better than "khamst" (keep a few khamst). 2 = shahrain / jem3ten (dual).
- (2026-11-19) Counts: once "marra wa7de", twice "martain / martein", 3+ "{n} marrat".
- (2026-11-16) Beginning of the month: "bi awal el shaher" is more common than "bi awalt el shaher" (both used); meaning decided: days 1-10 of this month.
- (2026-11-16) Periods decided: el sene el madye = last calendar year; mn sentain la hala2 / ekher sentain = 2 years ago to today; mn awal(t) el sene la hala2 = 1 Jan to today; ekher kam jem3a = last 21 days; mn el sayfiye la hala2 = 1 June of the latest summer to today; bl sayf = June-August of the latest summer.
- (2026-11-22) **"bi ekher heda el shaher"** = the end of THIS month; **"bi ekher hedek / hedak el shaher"** = the end of THAT month (one named earlier in the chat); **"b ekher shaher teshreen"** = the end of the month teshreen.
- (2026-11-16) Last week / last month: **ekher jemaa / ekher shaher** very common (also e5er). Last year: **ekher sene** common.
- (2026-11-16) This year so far: "**hal sene / hay el sene / hay l sene**" is more common than "mn awal el sene".
- (2026-11-15) abel mbereh / awalt mbereh = day before yesterday; ekher yawmein = last 2 days; men mberha la lyom = since yesterday; el taleta el madi = last Tuesday (el madi/el madye = that passed); haydik el jemaa = last week; bi ardit el jemaa = middle of the week; hal fatra = lately/this while; la hadit halla2 = until now.
- (2026-11-22) Until now: **"la hadit hala2"** too (a few "la hadit halla2" are fine).
- (2026-11-14) Yesterday: mberha is as natural as mbere7.
- (2026-11-22) "el jem3a li ra7et" is usually last WEEK, sometimes last Friday (nhar el jem3a = Friday): no need to hyperfocus, maybe one example meaning the day. [flagged: two meanings by her own words: kept as written]
- (2026-11-22) Last Friday (the day): "aday sarafet nhar el jem3a li ata3 / li ra7?" approved.

## 6. Family words and "both"

Questions about another person's spending are refused (UNSUPPORTED): the receipts are the user's own.

- (2026-11-20) Other people (their spending -> UNSUPPORTED): bayye / baye, 3ami, 3amti, khalti, khali, rfi2e, rfi2te, mama, baba, ekhte, sohri, eben 3ame, bent 3ame, bent khalte, eben khalti, jawze, marti, emme, khayi, jarna, her own: khalto, aamto / 3amto, 3amo, khalo ("khalo baado aam bi dakhin?"), and a name ("how much Ali spent": not the user).
- (2026-11-23) Family words are standalone ("marti" = my wife, "zawje" = my husband, "ekhte", "khayye", "ahle", "rfi2e"); as a follow-up ("w marti?") they mean that person's spending -> UNSUPPORTED. Approved short refused follow-ups: w marti? / w zawje? / w ekhte? / w khayye? / w ahle? / w rfi2e? / w el shaher el jeye? / w bokra? / w ma3ashe? / w el retib? / w el budget?
- (2026-11-16) Friend: rfi2te (f, "aday sarafet rfi2te"), rfi2e (m, "aday saraf rfi2e"), ref2ati (pl, "aday sarafo ref2ati").
- (2026-11-22) "both" as an answer ("Mazloum aw Nassar?" -> both): **tnayneton / tnainetin / el tnen / l tnayn**.
- (2026-11-22) "all three" = **tleteton**, "all four" = **arb3eton** (like tnayneton for both).

## 8. Varying phrasing

Users vary spelling, wording and laziness; replies should too, but only among approved forms.

- (2026-11-19 (phrasing)) "its either correct OR varied with you, never both".
- (undated (phrasing)) never use a phrase she has not approved or seen as if it were common
- (undated (phrasing)) keep formal words rare ("zoret"); vary months, periods and sentence shapes; include lazy short answers.
- (2026-11-20 (phrasing)) Vary EVERY common word, not only the one the set is about
- (2026-11-20 (phrasing)) adde / aday / adey / adeysh / addesh / 2adesh; where: wen / wain / wayn; day before: abel / abl / 2abel / awalt.
- (2026-11-15) Adding receipts: vary sajalet / sayavet / hatayt; receipt counts: vary aday sajalna / aday eende / aday mawjud / aday hatayna — never default to sajjalna.
- (2026-11-15) "paid for it": aday / adde / adaysh dafa3et 3alay / 3leh / aalay, so vary them.
- (2026-11-20) keep them as variety ("arabic has a million ways")
- (2026-11-19) Vary months (not always nisan).
- (2026-11-22) "the things I bought": vary **yali / li + jebton / jebta / jebto**, not only "li jebton".
